sources.headline: Yemeni military says it has retaken Mokha and 'secured' Red Sea waterway
sources.text: Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia say they have retaken control of the Red Sea port city of Mokha and "secured" the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the start of a major offensive against the Iran-backed Houthi movement.The Yemeni military said National Shield, Giants Brigades and Tihama Resistance forces had captured Mokha on Monday afternoon with the help of Saudi air strikes.Hours earlier, the military said its forces had seized Dhubab airport, 45km (27 miles) to the south, and were besieging Houthi fighters inside the nearby town.There was no immediate comment from the Houthis, but Houthi-run media denied that government forces had made advances in Dhubab.The government said operations had also begun on other fronts on Monday, including the capital Sanaa, which fell to the Houthis at the start of the civil war 12 years ago.Meanwhile, a Saudi-led military coalition said its fighter jets were providing "round-the-clock" air support to the pro-government forces and had destroyed 324 "high-value" targets since the start of the offensive.Saudi air strikes killed a schoolgirl and a woman in the Sanhan and Saawan districts of Sanaa on Monday, according to Houth-run Al Masirah TV.Houthi spokesman Mohammed Abdul Salam said Saudi Arabia was committing "dozens of massacres" and that it must "bear all the consequences".The Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Co-ordination Centre warned civilian airlines that Saudi airspace, except for the skies above the Islamic holy cities of Mecca and Medina, was no longer safe because it had become "a theatre of operations".On Sunday, the head of Yemen's internationally recognised Presidential Leadership Council announced the beginning of an offensive, dubbed Operation Yemen Dawn, aimed at retaking all territory held by the Houthis.Rashad al-Alimi insisted that all opportunities for de-escalation had been exhausted and called on all forces to carry out their assigned missions "until the country is liberated from the grip of the Houthi terrorist militia".It came after the Houthis reportedly cut a mountain road near the south-western city of Taiz, effectively leaving government forces and residents there surrounded.The Houthis also said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at oil facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia in retaliation for dozens of Saudi strikes on their territory.According to BBC Verify, satellite imagery from Saturday shows thick, dark smoke coming from the site of a strike at the Aramco Riyadh Refinery, in the city's south-east.A similar plume of smoke can be seen rising from the Khurais Central Processing Facility as well as from a potential strike point in satellite imagery from Sunday.Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.Last month, the Houthis launched a surprise offensive along Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and quickly ousted pro-government forces from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, including Mokha, Dhubab and Perim (Mayyun) Island.They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.However, the seizure of the strait contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.At least 959 people have been killed and 5,000 injured in the fighting in Yemen since 6 August, according to the government's health ministry.The UN says another 197,000 people have been displaced.

sources.headline: Saudi-backed forces recapture key areas around strait from Houthis in Yemen
sources.text: Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around Bab al-Mandab strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, Yemeni officials said on Monday.The officials said forces allied with the internationally recognized government have retaken the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns.The government push came as part of a major offensive launched early Monday under an air cover by a Saudi military coalition, aiming to retake all territory held by the Houthis.However, the offensive came just after the rebels said they had captured more territory in the south-western part of Yemen, taking the key town of Turbah in a blow to the Saudi-backed forces as they advanced toward the strategic provincial capital of Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city.The Saudi-led coalition spokesperson, Maj Gen Turki al-Malki, said 100 fighter jets were providing support to the forces of Yemen’s internationally recognized government fighting against the Houthis. He said the coalition had secured “air protection” of the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets as part of the ongoing campaign.Marco Rubio told reporters that it was expected that the Saudi-backed government in Yemen would hit back at the rebels to reclaim territory. Asked if the Saudi-led coalition coordinated the action with the United States, the US secretary of state said that Saudi Arabia and the US had a defense agreement but would not offer more details.He said the Yemeni government was ousted from some of its territory by a Houthi campaign and the Saudis had come under attack, and “they have a right to defend themselves”.The new push sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait – a chokepoint for international shipping – after a lightning offensive by the Iran-backed Houthis.Yemen’s internationally recognised government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have increasingly targeted Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, and on Sunday said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital again.The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government’s interim capital, Aden, according to four security sources.The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around the city.“We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station,” a police source in the area said.Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city. Fighting in the area was ongoing, they added.Sources from both sides told AFP on Sunday that fighting in and around the western province of Taiz had killed more than 70 people over the past day.Sources from the internationally recognised government reported that 34 government troops were killed – 20 on the edge of Taiz province in neighbouring Lahj – while Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in border areas with Lahj.Taiz city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen’s long-running civil war.A Houthi military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said on Sunday the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at the Saudi energy company Aramco’s sites in Riyadh and in the Khurais area in the east, causing large fires.The attacks were in response to what the Houthis claimed were 50 Saudi-led ‌air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours.There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.Saudi oil exports were already under pressure due to Iran’s blockade of the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.The Houthi’s Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes on Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded.With Reuters and Agence France-Presse

sources.headline: Can Yemen retake territory seized by Houthis?
sources.text: Inside StoryYemen’s government has launched an operation to retake territory held by the Houthis and restore its full control of the country.The Iran-backed Houthi rebel force, also known as Ansar Allah, has made significant territorial gains in the past month, seizing large areas on the Red Sea coast.In response, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan have met to discuss the situation in Yemen.In August, they signed a joint defence pact, which is being tested by this conflict.So, what are the regional dynamics at play?Will the counteroffensive by Yemen’s internationally recognised government achieve anything on the ground?Presenter: Neave BarkerGuests:Abdulaziz AlGhashian – Senior non-resident fellow at the Gulf International ForumSama’a Al Hamdani – Independent political analyst focusing on Yemen and the GCCTimothy Lenderking – Former US special envoy for Yemen and former deputy assistant secretary of state for Arabian Peninsula affairsPublished On 5 Oct 2026

sources.text:
7m ago
U.S. forces destroyed 13 commercial ships in Strait of Hormuz in recent months, CENTCOM says
The U.S. military destroyed 13 commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz over the past 12 weeks, U.S. Central Command said in a statement Monday.CENTCOM said the commercial vessels were either violating the U.S. Navy's blockade of the waterway, which resumed nearly three months ago under President Trump's direction, or were part of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' multibillion-dollar shadow network.Since July 14, U.S. forces have disabled three ships that refused to comply and redirected 130 commercial vessels attempting to pass through the strait, according to CENTCOM.
37m ago
Saudi Arabia and allies say their coalition attacked military targets in Yemen
A Saudi Arabia-led coalition in Yemen said Monday it had struck "military targets" belonging to the Houthis in Hodeida on the Red Sea coast.Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki said on X that its naval forces had "destroyed weapons depots, facilities storing booby-trapped boats and naval mines" and had "thwarted a planned attack" targeting waterways in the southern Red Sea.The Yemeni military said it carried out more than 1,000 strikes and began an offensive against the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the internationally recognized government said 100 warplanes flew sorties at dawn.The government had announced on Sunday the lofty goal of retaking all Houthi territory — home to most of Yemen's population, and much of it held for more than a decade.Last month, the Iran-backed group seized swathes of coastline along the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a chokepoint for oil and cargo shipping, in Yemen's deadliest fighting in years.
3:24 PM
Turkey, Pakistan to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia amid escalating Houthi attacks
Turkey and Pakistan will undertake a "rapid deployment" of troops to Saudi Arabia as part of a new mutual defense alliance, the three countries said Monday, as the Gulf kingdom faces escalating attacks from Yemen's Houthis.Following a meeting in Riyadh, the trio agreed "to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defense commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom," according to a joint statement.
2:57 PM
Iran president calls U.S. negotiations "meaningless," state media reports
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said negotiations with the U.S. were "meaningless" and only resulted in renewed attacks, state media reported, with progress on ending the Middle East war stalled for months."So far, they have attacked us three times after talks, and this shows that they are not seeking dialogue; rather, their goal is to overthrow the Islamic Republic of Iran," Pezeshkian was quoted as saying by the state news agency IRNA on Monday."With an enemy that every day resorts to assassination, sanctions, pressure and threats, and that breaks its commitments, negotiations are meaningless."Negotiations have effectively been at an impasse since Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz prompted the U.S. to resume military operations, and recent indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly failed to produce a breakthrough.After the U.S. scaled back military operations in September, favoring economic pressure instead, Iran's top diplomat said Sunday that the war would not be resolved through military action or new sanctions.Vowing that Iran would respond with a stronger defense if attacks resumed, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that "only negotiations based on justice and fairness could end the conflict."CBS/AFP
2:43 PM
Direct flights between Iraq and Iran to resume this week, airline says
Iraqi Airways will resume direct flights to Iran starting Thursday, the airline announced Monday, according to Iraq's Ministry of Transport.The airline said its "new operating plan will include regular daily flights" between Najaf International Airport, in central Iraq, and major Iranian airports in Mashhad, Tehran and Isfahan.The move comes as part of efforts by Iraq's Ministry of Transport to "reactivate air transport" and strengthen air connectivity between Iraq and regional destinations.According to the ministry's statement, the move to restore flights to Iran aims to "enhance the smooth flow of passengers" and provide "regular air transport options between Iraq and Iranian cities."
2:26 PM
Trump blames Ukraine strikes on Russian oil infrastructure for driving up gas prices instead of Iran war
President Trump on Monday blamed Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries for high gas prices, insisting that the Iran war was no longer responsible."What's driving up Gasoline is no longer the Strait of Hormuz, because Record Numbers of Barrels are coming out now on an almost daily basis, but the word, 'Refineries,' where Russia's are being blown up by Ukraine," Mr. Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.Mr. Trump also blamed what he said was the closing of oil refineries in California, led by Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom, with whom the president has a longstanding political rivalry. His comments came as the Republican Party potentially faces losing control of Congress after the November midterm elections.CBS/AFP
2:04 PM
Iranian interior minister travels to Doha for talks with Qatari counterpart
Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni traveled to Doha on Monday, where he'd been invited by his Qatari counterpart to meet with senior Qatari officials. Momeni was scheduled to meet and hold talks with Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Qatar's interior minister, according to Iran's Interior Ministry's Information Center. The center said Momeni would also meet with several other Qatari officials during the visit, joined by a delegation of Iranian Interior Ministry officials and governors who accompanied him.
